title: Police disrupt 57 illegal streaming services with 7.3 million visits
content_md: Law enforcement authorities from 11 countries have disrupted 57 illegal streaming services that operated hundreds of websites and drew over 7.3 million visits each year. Such illegal IPTV services offer access to television channels, live sports, and movies without permission from the copyright owners for a small monthly fee. According to the European Audiovisual Anti-Piracy Alliance (AAPA) trade association, legitimate service providers lose around €4.83 billion annually as roughly 60 million people in Europe use illegal platforms for streaming content. "The operation resulted in the disruption of 57 illegal IPTV services and the identification of 321 websites illegally offering copyrighted content, with a combined annual traffic of more than 7.3 million visits. Investigators have so far traced over EUR 26 million in cryptocurrency transactions, with further analysis ongoing," Europol said in a Tuesday press release. "The operation targeted a criminal market worth billions of euros annually, in which illegal streaming providers sell unauthorised access to premium television channels, live sports and films, often collecting subscription payments through cryptocurrency."
